note: Engager has central modern meanings hire/employ, engage/commit, and involve. The current pawn/enlist senses are valid but omit the most useful learner meanings.
proposed_english: to hire; to employ; to engage; to commit; to involve; to enlist; to pawn (context-dependent)

note: Gueule is informal and can be rude/vulgar when used for a person's face or mouth. The register warning should be explicit.
proposed_english: mouth/muzzle; face or mouth (informal, often rude); gob/mug (informal/rude)

note: Excuse is not only the noun 'excuse'; it is also a common present-tense and imperative form of excuser, including Excuse-moi. The gloss mentions these forms but POS does not.
proposed_english: excuse; excuses/is excusing; excuse! (forms of excuser, context-dependent)
proposed_pos: noun / finite verb form / imperative form

note: Riche must include the basic adjective meaning rich/wealthy. The current gloss gives secondary senses but omits the central learner meaning.
Course is also extremely common in faire les courses / les courses for shopping, errands, or groceries. That everyday plural use should be included.
proposed_english: race; run/running; errand; shopping/groceries (especially plural: les courses)

note: Bête is both the noun beast/animal and the very common adjective stupid/silly/foolish. The adjective is omitted despite adjective POS being listed.
Risque is a noun but also a common finite and imperative form of risquer. The current definition mentions those forms without reflecting them in POS.
proposed_english: risk; risks/is risking; risk! (forms of risquer, context-dependent)
proposed_pos: noun / finite verb form / imperative form

note: Officier is both the noun officer and the verb 'to officiate'. Verb POS is already listed but the verb meaning is missing.
Attaque is the noun attack/assault and also a common finite/imperative form of attaquer. The current POS lists only noun.
proposed_english: attack; assault; aggression; attacks/is attacking; attack! (forms of attaquer, context-dependent)
proposed_pos: noun / finite verb form / imperative form

note: Juge is both the noun judge and a common finite/imperative form of juger. The learner entry should not hide that homograph.
proposed_english: judge; judges/is judging; judge! (forms of juger, context-dependent)
